title: Not So Fast
summary:
Not So Fast
After last week's stock market tumble, many individuals and businesses paused to think about the stability and autonomy of the US and Chinese economies. The drop that was precipitated by other stock market declines in the Far East, left many wondering whether or not recent strength in the market was based on fundamentals or was simply a result of momentum. While the market has recovered slightly over the last several trading days, it still remains slightly lower than beginning of the year levels.

children.summary: S&P 500 Although the stock markets have taken a dip, freight rates have remained firm and both crude oil and refined product demand have continued to stay at record levels. With many quick to believe that long- running strength in the freight and equity markets are doomed to come to an end, there is reason to believe that growth will at least continue in the near-term.

children.summary: Volatility and sensitivity to momentum are two ubiquitous themes in the equity markets and are also constantly present in the freight markets. The chart below shows the Poten Tanker Index versus the Poten Tanker Equity Index.

children.title: PTI Index
children.summary: The public tanker companies appear to be on an upward trend overall, despite being impacted by the stock market decline at the end of February. Even more recently, especially in the past week, the freight markets have been improving across the board for tankers.
